pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Large, irregular polygonal dark regions on the dorsal midline transitioning to smaller, more fragmented patches on the lateral flank. Edges show moderate pixel-gradient softness with low-frequency angularity.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Continuous network of light-colored interstitial pathways. Junction nodes are primarily tri-radial. Pathway thickness is non-uniform, appearing wider along the dorsal spine and narrowing significantly as they descend the flank.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: The mane exhibits a low-amplitude, high-frequency serrated 1D silhouette against the background, extending from the upper neck through the shoulder ridge.
dorsal_ridge_profile.contour_gaps: Significant structural discontinuities are present where the mane line is interrupted by an external biological agent (oxpecker) and several raised nodular growths.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: Multiple raised, dark, cauliflower-textured masses are visible on the dorsal ridge and upper flank, exhibiting hyper-pigmentation and localized textural disruption.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent nodular lesions and irregular growths are distributed along the dorsal ridge, potentially representing parasitic or viral cutaneous anomalies.
other_distinctive_markers: Presence of a single oxpecker bird perched on the mid-dorsal ridge.
